title: The Lord Bless You and Keep You

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Tell Aaron and his sons, 'This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them: "The Lord bless you and keep you."'" - Num 6:22-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now comes one of the most beloved blessings in the whole Bible. God Himself gives the priests the very words to speak over His people. Think of that: these are not words humans invented to describe what they hoped God might do. These are God's own words of blessing, given to be spoken over His people. This is how God wants to relate to those who are His.

"The Lord bless you and keep you." To be blessed by God is to have His favour resting upon your life. And to be kept by God is to be guarded, protected, held safe in His care. What a comfort — the God who blesses is also the God who keeps.

We live in an uncertain world, and we cannot keep ourselves safe from every danger. But God can. The word "keep" pictures a watchful guardian who never sleeps, holding His people through every season. "The Lord will keep you from all harm—he will watch over your life" (Ps 121:7).

This blessing was spoken over God's old covenant people, and its heart still stands for all who belong to God through Christ. In Jesus, we are blessed "with every spiritual blessing" (Eph 1:3), and He keeps us so securely that nothing can snatch us from His hand (John 10:28-29).

Receive these words over your own life today: the Lord bless you, and the Lord keep you. Rest in the favour and the safekeeping of your God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What does it mean to you that God wants to bless and keep you?
- Where do you need to trust God as the One who "keeps" you?
- How does being kept in Christ give you security?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You bless and keep Your people. Let Your favour rest on my life, and hold me safe in Your care today. Amen.
